correctness.rationale: PASS: In the actual finite subgroup H generated by the supports, character idempotents e_chi have norm one, orthogonal multiplication and sum to the group-algebra identity; this decomposition remains valid for arbitrary infinite-support targets in ℓ¹(G). At each Fourier corner, if z_chi zero inputs occur, replacing z-1 zero components by t e_chi and solving the last one divides an O(t^s) target by t^{z-1}, yielding O(t) input changes. Nonzero corners divide by a nonzero scalar. Summing over N corners costs at most N t, so with t=epsilon/(2N) the full target epsilon^s ball is attained. The upper bound uses a norm-one group character extending chi and a target perturbation along e_chi to force exponent s; s=1 is handled by telescoping. All finite-support tuples, arbitrary torsion abelian G and full ℓ¹ targets are covered; extension and H-independence valid. Exact finite checks corroborative, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: The complete k-fold sharp exponent s=max(1,max_chi number of simultaneously vanishing input Fourier coordinates) is not the two-factor zero/no-zero dichotomy of the published pair theorem. The new k>2 simultaneous-zero multiplicity exponents and constructive full ambient factorization remain distinct, although the extension is structurally close to classical idempotent splitting.
